Key Research Thinking Patterns: High-Throughput Functional Genomics: Systematic mapping of gene function and essentiality in anaerobic model organisms using large-scale transposon mutagenesis and fitness profiling. (e.g., Generating a Random Barcode Transposon-Site Sequencing (RB-TnSeq) library in Desulfovibrio vulgaris Hildenborough to assay fitness across 244 growth conditions, identifying 1,137 conditional phenotype genes and novel vitamin synthesis pathways.)

Temporal Correlation and Early Warning Modeling: Leveraging time-series analysis of environmental samples to predict and detect community-level disease outbreaks prior to clinical reporting. (e.g., Applying seasonal regression and cross-correlation matrix analysis to 18-month wastewater data for Salmonella, Campylobacter, and norovirus to demonstrate a 1-2 week lead time over traditional surveillance.)

Rapid Molecular Variant Surveillance: Utilizing targeted nucleic acid amplification techniques as cost-effective alternatives to genomic sequencing for tracking pathogen evolution and demographic spread. (e.g., Deploying allele-specific RT-qPCR assays to detect the SARS-CoV-2 Omicron variant in Oklahoma wastewater two weeks before official reports, correlating emergence with socioeconomic factors.)

Methodological Validation and Selectivity Assessment: Rigorous evaluation of the specificity and accuracy of commercial or standard environmental assays to ensure reliable data interpretation in complex matrices. (e.g., Testing the IDEXX Enterolert fluorogenic substrate method in freshwater sediments to identify false positives from Paenibacillus spp., demonstrating the method's lack of exclusivity for Enterococcus in non-fecal environments.)
Summary Description: Kara B. De León is a principal investigator specializing in the intersection of anaerobic microbial physiology and public health surveillance. Her research employs high-throughput functional genomics, specifically Random Barcode Transposon-Site Sequencing (RB-TnSeq), to characterize the metabolic capabilities and essential gene sets of sulfate-reducing bacteria like Desulfovibrio vulgaris, with applications in bioremediation and industrial corrosion. Concurrently, she pioneers wastewater-based epidemiology (WBE) to monitor infectious diseases, utilizing quantitative PCR, digital PCR, and time-series statistical modeling to detect gastrointestinal pathogens and SARS-CoV-2 variants. Her work provides critical early warning capabilities for public health interventions by correlating environmental pathogen loads with clinical outbreak data, while also validating the selectivity of standard water quality assays to improve the accuracy of environmental monitoring.
